data.symptom: Orders are held in Payment pending although the customer paid once, and two customers were charged twice. Every affected order's first payment answer took longer than checkout's 8 second timeout.
impact: 9 tickets on 9 orders from 3 channels over 21 days.
Held orders missed their pick list and their delivery promise.
2 customers were charged twice for one order.

evidence.point: Every affected order's first answer took 8.4 to 13.9 s, over the 8 s timeout.
The second attempt went out with a new idempotency key, so the processor made a second authorization.
evidence.quote: extra authorization au_96FA on a captured order

evidence.point: The app's automatic retry raced the first answer, and both authorizations were captured.
11 of 25 slow first answers in 21 days led to a second authorization; no checkout answered under 8 s was affected.

hypotheses.statement: Checkout makes a new idempotency key for each attempt, so a retry after a slow answer creates a second authorization, and the order service holds or double-captures the order.
supports: Two keys for one order in the #51102 log.
Every affected order's first answer took over 8 s.
against_or_gaps: The processor's own logs are not available to support.
Full logs exist for four of the nine orders.

hypotheses.statement: The processor sends authorization webhooks late or twice under load, which makes the order service hold orders. May coexist with the first.
supports: Every affected order had a slow first answer.
One held order (H-4109) never got its webhook.
against_or_gaps: Each extra authorization has its own key from our checkout.
H-4109 had one authorization and one key.

ruled_out: The processor or the card issuer duplicating
open_questions: Should checkout reuse one idempotency key for every retry of a checkout?
Should checkout look a payment up by key before showing an error?
How should the order service stop two captures for one order?

what_it_does_not_prove: That the real processor answers like the lab's scripted one.

keep_watching: Orders held for another reason, like a lost webhook.
data.next_decision: Keep the flag on the canary store for another 14 days; widen only if second authorizations stay at zero and declined cards still get a new key. A double capture on the canary reverses it.

data.title: Order stuck in Payment pending with a second authorization after a slow checkout
applies_when: Order says Payment pending although the customer paid once.
Customer's bank shows two pending holds for one order.
Checkout showed an error after a long spin, and the customer paid again.
how_to_confirm: Processor: two authorizations for the order, each with its own idempotency key.
Checkout log: the first answer came after the 8 s timeout.
Processor: exactly one capture for the order.
steps: Confirm the payment processor shows one capture for the order, before RB-21.
Apply RB-21: release the hold and void the extra authorization.
Link the ticket to the parent incident and tell the customer the extra hold drops off.
Flag the order for a payments review and note the voided authorization.
escalate_if: The processor shows two settled captures.
Only one authorization exists, as when a webhook was lost.
A fraud flag is on the order.
data.status_note: ENG-5230 is on the canary store; until it is on everywhere, slow payments still create second authorizations.
